questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the idiom/phrase.**

To have at one's fingertips

options.text: To be very fast on the keyboard.
To be adroit with a percussion musical instrument.
Recall of factual information at one's command.
To carefully note down minute details.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3.

**'To have at one's fingertips'** means **'at one's command or disposal, as recall of factual information'.**

Example: She had everybody's contact numbers at her fingertips.

Protection of or authority over someone
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

The meanings of the given words are:

 
• Autonomous: having the freedom to act independently.
 
• For Example, They proudly declared themselves part of a new autonomous province.
 
• Tutelage: Protection of or authority over someone or something; guardianship.
 
• For Example, He succeeded his father in 1112 and was placed under the tutelage of his mother.

• For Example: Since his accident, he hasn't been able to walk unaided

Hence, the correct answer is **'tutelage'**.

questions.question:
**In the following question, a sentence has been given in Active/Passive Voice. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Active/Passive Voice.**

Who taught you to ride?

options.text: By whom is you taught to ride?
By whom were you taught to ride?
Riding by you was taught by who?
Riding by you was taught by whom?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2.

The given sentence is in the Active Voice as the form of the verb (‘taught’) shows that its subject (‘you’) did something and was ‘active’.

Therefore, it has to be changed to the Passive voice, where something was done by the subject, and it was ‘passive’.

In order to do that,

a. The object of the transitive verb (the verb which uses more than one objects) in the Active voice should become the subject of the verb in the Passive voice.

b. The verb should be changed from the Active voice to the Passive voice without changing its tense.

Thus, the same sentence in the Passive voice is **‘By whom were you taught to ride?'**

questions.question:
**In the following question, a sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect Speech. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct Speech.**

Sheetal said to me, "How have you solved this problem?"

options.text: Sheetal asked me how I had solved that problem.
Sheetal asked me how I have solved that problem.
Sheetal asked me how I had solved this problem.
Sheetal asked me how I have solved this problem.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sheetal asked me how I had solved that problem. **__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Let us begin by identifying the kind of sentence. It is an interrogative sentence. (Wh-Question)
 
• The reporting verb ‘said to’ should be changed as ‘asked’ in indirect speech.
 
• Following that, we need to remove the commas and inverted commas as we change it into an indirect speech.
 
• The Question is changed into assertive form and is simply placed after the reporting verb.
 
• The question mark is also removed.

Correct answer: *Sheetal asked me how I had solved that problem. *

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

When changing a direct speech to indirect speech:

 
• The words of the speaker are not enclosed in inverted commas.
 
• The conjunction ‘that’ will not be used. (In case of interrogative sentence)
 
• To make an indirect speech of Wh -Questions, The Question is changed into assertive form and is simply placed after the reporting verb.
 
• To make an indirect speech of YES/NO-Questions, if or whether will be used.
 
• The question mark is also removed.
 
• e.g., DIRECT: He said to me, “Will you help me?”

 INDIRECT: He asked me if I would help him.

 
• DIRECT: He said to me, “Why are you late?”

 INDIRECT: He asked me why I am late.

Since when (have to start) a business been so easy?

The correct answer is **Has starting**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**
